To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a mobile platform for rapid sub pg/mL, multiplexed digital droplet detection was developed and characterized with recombinant proteins, and endogenous cytokines in human serum, and showed excellent correlation to the gold standard system.

we developed an ultrasensitive, mobile platform for multiplex digital detection of proteins in serum, that is based on parallelized droplet generation, time domain encoded mobile imaging, and on chip sample processing.
we developed a mobile platform for rapid sub-pg/mL multiplexed digital droplet assays.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a mobile digital droplet assay platform for the rapid and multiplexed analysis of proteins in serum.
the miniaturization of digital assays into a low cost mobile platform that enables multiplexing and ultrasensitive detection.
the development of an optofluidsic device capable of performing digital assays on a mobile phone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have successfully demonstrated a mobile digital assay for multiplexed detection of proteins.
we developed a mobile platform for rapid sub pg/mL, multiplexed digital droplet detection that is >1000x faster than conventional digital ELISA.
we have developed a mobile digital assay platform that is >1000x faster than conventional digital assays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a mobile digital droplet platform for the rapid detection of proteins in serum.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to develop a mobile platform to perform a digital ELISA that is >1,000x more sensitive than a standard ELISA and is compatible with complex media.
we have developed a mobile digital assay platform that can be used for the rapid and sensitive detection of multiple proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
digital droplet assays can be miniaturized to a mobile format, with ultrasensitivity, and multiplexing capabilities.
digital assays can be miniaturized to a mobile format, which can be used for point of care applications, and that this approach can achieve the same sensitivity as laboratory based digital assays.
we developed an optically integrated microfluidic device that is >1000x faster than conventional droplet detection and can be used to perform multiplexed digital immunoassays in minutes.
